3.old: Sardis East Vedder is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
3.new: The City of Chilliwack has no published boundary for Sardis East Vedder, which is a sub-area name used in the MLS®.

4.old: The closest official descriptions are the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which covers Sardis as a whole, and the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan, which names Vedder Road as its western boundary.
4.new: For anything official, the nearest thing is a pair of plans. The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan takes in all of Sardis, while the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan puts its western edge at Vedder Road.

34.old: Browse Sardis East Vedder homes for sale in Chilliwack, BC. View MLS listings, prices and neighbourhood info for this Chilliwack community.
34.new: Homes for sale in Sardis East Vedder, Chilliwack, BC: see current MLS listings, prices and neighbourhood details for this Chilliwack community.

39.old: Chilliwack is in School District 33 (SD33). SD33’s Long Range Facilities Plan says its elementary schools are kindergarten to grade 5, its middle schools grades 6 to 8 and its secondary schools grades 9 to 12.
39.new: Schools here fall under School District 33 (SD33) in Chilliwack. According to the district’s Long Range Facilities Plan, elementary runs from kindergarten to grade 5, middle school covers grades 6 to 8, and secondary school covers grades 9 to 12.

98.old: Published municipal records do not list a separate statement of typical home types for Sardis East Vedder in published municipal records. City plan documents state land-use policy, not the housing that is already built
98.new: Sardis East Vedder has no separate statement of typical home types in the municipal records the City has published. What the City’s plan documents set out is land-use policy, and that is a different thing from the housing already built.

102.old: Lot size (FVREB MLS® recorded sales data): the median lot size of detached houses sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity was 5,231 sq ft, based on 7 sales with a recorded lot size.
102.new: Looking at FVREB MLS® recorded sales data for lot size, the median lot for detached houses that sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity came to 5,231 sq ft. That figure rests on 7 sales that had a recorded lot size.

120.old: The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan covers Sardis, including this area. Council adopted it on January 5, 2021, as OCP Schedule D, through Official Community Plan Amendment Bylaw 2020, No. 5024.
120.new: This area falls inside the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which applies to Sardis generally. The plan became OCP Schedule D when Council adopted it on January 5, 2021, by way of Bylaw No. 5024, the 2020 amendment to the Official Community Plan.

121.old: The South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan covers the area just south of this sub-area. Council adopted it in 2022 and it was updated in 2025 with the Official Community Plan.
121.new: Just to the south of Sardis East Vedder is the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan area. Council adopted the plan in 2022 and then updated it in 2025, when the Official Community Plan was updated too.

122.old: The South Vedder plan area is bordered by the Chilliwack River and Vedder River to the south, the Promontory neighbourhood to the southeast, Tzeachten First Nations Lands to the east, Vedder Road to the west and the Vedder neighbourhood to the north.
122.new: Around the South Vedder plan area, Vedder Road is its western edge and the Vedder neighbourhood its northern one. Tzeachten First Nations Lands are on the east, the Promontory neighbourhood is southeast, and the Chilliwack River and Vedder River form the southern limit.

124.old: Slope and ground: this area sits on the Vedder alluvial fan. A BC Government study describes the Sardis–Vedder Aquifer under it as unconfined cobbles, gravel and sand.
124.new: Slope and ground: Sardis East Vedder is on the Vedder alluvial fan. The Sardis–Vedder Aquifer beneath it, according to a BC Government study, is unconfined cobbles, gravel and sand.

125.old: The same study says the fan slopes from 36 m elevation near its head to 12 m where it reaches the Fraser floodplain, and that the City’s well field at the head of the fan is the main domestic water supply.
125.new: The study adds that elevation on the fan falls from 36 m near the head to 12 m by the time it meets the Fraser floodplain. It also says the main domestic water supply comes from the City’s well field, which is at the fan’s head.

126.old: Floodplain: the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates the floodplains of the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and the Vedder Canal, plus the alluvial fans and floodplains of several creeks. It sets building setbacks of 75 m from the natural boundary of the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River.
126.new: Floodplain rules come from Bylaw 2018, No. 4519, the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw. It designates the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder river floodplains and the Vedder Canal, along with several creeks’ alluvial fans and floodplains. Setbacks for buildings are 75 m, measured from the Vedder River’s natural boundary, while the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River call for 30 m.

128.old: The City keeps flood response plans for both the Fraser River and the Vedder River, and runs an ongoing $30 million dyke-raising program.
128.new: The City maintains flood response plans covering the Fraser River as well as the Vedder River, alongside a $30 million dyke-raising program that is still going.

132.old: If the home is near the Vedder River, Vedder Canal or a creek, ask the City how the floodplain bylaw and its setbacks apply to the exact lot.
132.new: For a home close to the Vedder River, the Vedder Canal or a creek, it’s worth asking the City how its floodplain bylaw and setbacks apply to that specific lot.

157.old: That is an orientation from addresses, not a City boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
157.new: Treat that as a rough orientation from addresses, not a City boundary, and ask me whether a given address is in it.

173.old: The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which Council adopted on January 5, 2021, as OCP Schedule D (Bylaw 2020, No. 5024).
173.new: The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, adopted by Council as OCP Schedule D on January 5, 2021 under Bylaw 2020, No. 5024.

176.old: The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 designates the floodplains of the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and the Vedder Canal, plus the alluvial fans and floodplains of several creeks. It sets setbacks of 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River.
176.new: Bylaw 4519, the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw, covers floodplains along the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers, the Vedder Canal, and several creeks’ alluvial fans and floodplains. Required setbacks: 75 m along the Vedder River, and a smaller 30 m beside the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River.
